COVID-19 outcomes in strict-border and open-border countries

covid_border.Rd

Daily COVID-19 case and death rates for six countries between March 2020 and December 2023. Three of them (Australia, New Zealand and China) kept strict border quarantine in place for most of the pandemic. The other three (the United Kingdom, the United States and Sweden) did not.

Usage

covid_border

Format

A data frame with 8,406 rows and 7 columns:

country

Country name, as a factor.

date

Date of the observation.

cases_per_million

New confirmed cases per million people, as a seven-day rolling average.

deaths_per_million

New confirmed deaths per million people, as a seven-day rolling average.

vaccinated_pct

Share of the population fully vaccinated, in per cent. Carried forward between reporting dates, and zero before the rollout began.

population

Country population.

border_strategy

Whether the country used strict border control, as a factor with two levels.

Source

Our World in Data COVID-19 dataset, licensed CC BY 4.0: https://docs.owid.io/projects/etl/api/covid/. Prepared by data-raw/covid_border.R.

Examples

head(covid_border)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 7
#>   country   date       cases_per_million deaths_per_million vaccinated_pct
#>   <fct>     <date>                 <dbl>              <dbl>          <dbl>
#> 1 Australia 2020-03-01            0.0164            0                    0
#> 2 Australia 2020-03-02            0.0382            0.00545              0
#> 3 Australia 2020-03-03            0.0382            0.00545              0
#> 4 Australia 2020-03-04            0.0545            0.0109               0
#> 5 Australia 2020-03-05            0.109             0.0109               0
#> 6 Australia 2020-03-06            0.185             0.0109               0
#> # ℹ 2 more variables: population <dbl>, border_strategy <fct>
table(covid_border$country)
#> 
#>      Australia    New Zealand          China United Kingdom  United States 
#>           1401           1401           1401           1401           1401 
#>         Sweden 
#>           1401
